Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Anoop Trivedi, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Sri Ankit Shukla, counsel for the applicant as well as Sri Nitin Kesharwani, learned Additional Government Advocate for State.
3.

The present application for anticipatory bail has been filed for protection in regard to Case Crime No.286 of 2004, under Sections 304-B, 498A I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S.
Sadar Bazar, District Shahjahanpur.
4.
As per prosecution story, the applicant and other co-accused persons are stated to have subjected the deceased person to cruelty for demand of dowry leading to her death on 26.04.2004.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Senior Counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is the brother-in-law of the deceased person and has been falsely implicated in the present case as he lives separately to the main accused person.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
The police had investigated the matter and a closure report was filed with respect to the applicant.
The applicant has been summoned by invoking the powers under Section 319 Cr.P.C. vide order dated 24.04.2008.
The applicant and other co-accused persons had challenged the said summoning order by filing Criminal Revision No.1350 of 2008 and the proceedings were stayed vide order dated 21.05.2008.

Learned Senior Counsel has further stated that the applicant is a bona fide person and came to know of the summons having been issued against the applicant only when the police came to his house in his search.
The said revision was dismissed vide order dated 02.12.2016 in default.
The applicant had no knowledge of the said dismissal order and he was not communicated with the said order either.
Applicant is ready to cooperate during trial.
He has no criminal antecedents to his credit.
6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application on the ground that the matter is of the year 2004 and 19 years have passed since then.
The applicant has not cooperated in trial.
He is enjoying the stay order since 2008, as such trial with respect to the other co-accused persons have also not been concluded as yet.
The applicant is not entitled for anticipatory bail.
Learned A.G.A. has also stated that there is criminal history of one case of the year 2003 assigned to the applicant which has not been explained.
7. In rebuttal, learned Senior Counsel has stated that the trial of the co-accused persons is nearing at its conclusion as it is fixed for arguments.

8. After arguing for some time, applicant's counsel submits that the present application for anticipatory bail may be disposed of with a direction to file a regular bail application which may be decided keeping in view the guidelines as laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another reported in 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another reported in 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. Learned A.G.A. has no objection to the prayer of learned counsel for the applicant.
10. After hearing learned counsel for the parties, no case is made out for interference U/s 438 Cr.P.C.

The present anticipatory bail application is disposed of with a direction that the applicant shall surrender before the concerned court within one month from today and in case a regular bail application is filed, the same be decided in view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in case of Satender Kumar Antil (supra).

11. For the period of one month from today or till the time of surrender of the applicant before the concerned court, whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant, in the above case.

(Krishan Pahal, J.) Order Date :- 22.5.2023 Ravi Kant  Ram Kishor Mishra vs State Of U.P. on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92940228/
